executiveSummary: GM1621's 2025 identity, centre, 61 neighbourhoods, three BAG places, six settlement labels, one ProRail station and eight normalized municipal-border road links are coherent, and the deterministic ten-preset, six-checkpoint, eight-service contract passes. Release is nevertheless correction-required. Lansingerland is a low, managed polder municipality divided between HHSK and Delfland: Polder Bleiswijk drains through De Kooi and Gemaal Lansingerland to the Rotte, the Rotte continues through Rotterdam and Gemaal Schilthuis to the Nieuwe Maas, regional kades and emergency storage matter, while Berkel has separate water-management dependencies. The generic river preset instead holds exactly 1.464364 m, 29,938 affected people-equivalent and every service value unchanged from T+24 through T+72 without a selected Rotte, downstream tidal/backwater, kering, breach, storage, arrival or recession event. The coastal and pluvial presets likewise produce precise local depths without their distinct boundary or rainfall/drainage evidence. Six hazard presets reuse the same population-led top five neighbourhoods. The graph correctly includes the now-open A16 and Rottemerentunnel corridor, A12 and N209/N470/N471 links, rail and metro context, but it does not model tunnel systems, internal access, event-time transit or cross-boundary acute-care destinations. Public registers identify 349 water assets, Stedin/Dunea/Ziggo point territories, one grid-planning sample, 98 antenna installations, 41 education records and no acute-care facility inside GM1621, but not operational topology, state, backup or restoration. Current HHSK/Delfland works and the dated Rottemeren fire-risk notice are context, not timeless scenario inputs. Unsupported consequence and recovery precision must be suppressed; missing, stale or horizon-limited values remain Unknown/NoData, never zero, safe, open or available.

evidenceSources.publisher: Centraal Bureau voor de Statistiek / PDOK / Kadaster
evidenceSources.title: E01 — GM1621 official 2025 municipality, neighbourhood, place and settlement geography and statistics
evidenceSources.edition: CBS Wijken en buurten 2025; generated source snapshots retrieved 31 August 2026
supports: The annual CC BY 4.0 CBS/PDOK input identifies GM1621 as Lansingerland and reports 66,064 residents, density 1,240/km², 16.8% aged 65 or older and 6,417 one-person households; the generated centre [4.49512896380311, 51.99958867798162] is inside the 2025 boundary.

Sixty-one neighbourhood rows in 16 districts sum to 66,055 residents, nine below the municipality total (-0.014%); households sum to 25,845 and rounded age-65-plus rows to 11,125. Deterministic allocation reconciles exactly to 66,064 without rewriting the published rows.

BAG supplies three active places—Bergschenhoek, Berkel en Rodenrijs and Bleiswijk—and every place centre is contained by the generalized municipality. BRT supplies six settlement labels: five woonkernen and one deelkern, including Kruisweg, Noordeinde and Rotte. BAG/PDOK place data are Public Domain Mark 1.0 and CBS/BRT are edition-based CC BY 4.0.

District-heating share and public-charging indicators cover 0/61 neighbourhoods; home value omits 12 rows, cars per household 16, several tenure/benefit fields ten and other fields fewer. Publisher null, suppression and non-applicability remain NoData, not zero; annual residents omit commuters, pupils, greenhouse workers, visitors, patients and incident-time occupancy.

evidenceSources.title: E02 — Leefomgevingsfoto Lansingerland 2.0: water, climate, infrastructure and greenhouse context
supports: The municipal baseline distinguishes present-state public-source context from a 2050 reference situation. It identifies three cores, a major greenhouse economy, low wet/subsiding ground, heat, heavy-rain and drought concerns; these are static/planning classes, not observations or a current forecast.

Its pluvial figure uses the Klimaateffectatlas 2021 70 mm in two hours approximately 1:100 scenario and says some places retain more than 15–20 mm on the street, potentially flooding basements/garages or making roads impassable. The province's 70 mm in one hour building standard has no corresponding map in the report. Neither scenario validates the simulator's 0.602696 m municipality scalar.

The baseline reports that greenhouse concentrations can create an unusually strong heat-island effect outside population cores and affect nearby housing, while drought can damage crops, increase nature-fire risk and oxidize peat. These maps/claims are dated exposure context and must not be treated as an event-time temperature, demand, ignition or consequence field.

The report describes A12 and provincial links and, at its publication date, the then-future A16 extension. Rijkswaterstaat's later 2025 opening evidence supersedes that lifecycle status. No standard blanket content or map-reuse licence was identified, so integration should use the cited underlying governed layers or explicit permission rather than scrape figures.

evidenceSources.publisher: Hoogheemraadschap van Schieland en de Krimpenerwaard / Het Waterschapshuis
evidenceSources.title: E03 — Polder Bleiswijk water system, wastewater dependency and public water-asset register
evidenceSources.edition: Current HHSK peil-decision explanation inspected 3 September 2026; HWH snapshot retrieved 3 September 2026 01:38Z
supports: HHSK states that all of Polder Bleiswijk drains to the Rotte through De Kooi and Gemaal Lansingerland. Higher areas route by weirs, lower areas by local pumping, and water from Polder Schiebroek also passes through the system; most supply comes from the Rotte while two southeastern level areas receive Delfland water.

Bergschenhoek buiten operates within a flexible -6.70 to -6.55 m NAP band and contains greenhouse, recreation/nature, agriculture and housing uses. A peil decision is static design/management context, not a live level, pump command, spare capacity or inundation forecast.

HHSK separately states that Kralingseveer in Capelle aan den IJssel treats wastewater from part of Lansingerland. This confirms a cross-boundary wastewater dependency but not its contributing catchment, current flow/state, power/backup, bypass, quality or restoration for a selected incident.

Full CBS-boundary containment assigns 349 HWH records: 28 sewer pumps, four sluices, 35 surface-water pumps and 282 weirs. Managers are HHSK 173, Delfland 148, Unknown 27 and third party one; 53 capacities are non-null and 296 null, while 327 are register-status gerealiseerd and 22 unknown. IMWA/DAMO is CC BY-SA 4.0 with contributor-dependent coverage; points, heterogeneous capacities and register status do not form a connected operational network.

evidenceSources.publisher: Hoogheemraadschap van Schieland en de Krimpenerwaard
evidenceSources.title: E04 — Current Eendragtspolder inlet works and downstream Rotte discharge chain
evidenceSources.edition: Notice dated 10 August 2026; works scheduled 17 August through approximately late September 2026
supports: HHSK says polder pumps discharge excess rainwater to the Rotte, which flows toward Rotterdam and is pumped by Schilthuis to the Nieuwe Maas; if the Rotte cannot discharge rainwater, the Eendragtspolder emergency storage can be activated. This is a cross-boundary hydraulic chain, not a municipality-local river-depth coefficient.

The emergency store is described as approximately four million m³, but the 2026 work changes inlet fill rate, not stated total storage. Works were scheduled for about four weeks from 17 August, so they overlap the audit reference time; project start and intended benefit do not prove completion, current usable inlet capacity or activation.

The Rottekade was to remain open, sometimes narrowed with traffic control. That published construction context does not specify exact restriction intervals or guaranteed emergency/freight throughput and must expire or become Unknown after its validity window.

No standard blanket reuse licence was identified on the public notice. A decision-facing adapter needs authoritative asset/event identifiers, lifecycle and operational state, issue/valid time, capacity unit, command authority and uncertainty before storage or pumping changes simulated consequences.

evidenceSources.title: E05 — Current Polder Berkel drought, dike, storage and water-quality actions
evidenceSources.edition: Operational updates through 31 August 2026; broader drought chronology through 28 August 2026
supports: Delfland stored extra freshwater during prolonged drought to limit lasting nature damage and keep dikes strong, then began controlled emptying of Bergboezem Berkel. At the 31 August update the cycle path had reopened after water receded, but emptying, oxygen monitoring and water-quality mitigation continued.

A temporary pump near Oude Leedeweg/Bovenmolenweg was expected to run daily 07:00–19:00 for two to three weeks from 26 August, and controlled emptying was expected to take up to three weeks depending on weather and pumping rate. This is dated operational context, not a timeless or guaranteed control state.

Delfland's 28 August chronology records repair of drought cracks at Leeweg in Polder Berkel and its 26–27 August updates changed withdrawal and lock restrictions. A completed repair or lifted measure does not establish all dikes safe, all water available or future conditions; each status requires an issue and expiry/valid time.

Delfland and HHSK jointly distinguish greenhouse water areas: Polder Berkel is within Delfland, while Bleiswijk and Bergschenhoek are HHSK. Monthly water-quality measurements, drought measures and greenhouse dependence are observation/planning context, not drinking-water quality, crop loss, supply availability or a municipal water-service percentage. No standard blanket reuse licence was identified.

evidenceSources.title: E06 — A16 Rottemerentunnel, NWB road corridors, rail station and public-transit context
evidenceSources.edition: A16/Rottemerentunnel opened October 2025; NWB-Light 1 August 2026; ProRail/GTFS deployment snapshots retrieved 2–3 September 2026
supports: Rijkswaterstaat says the 2.2 km, two-tube Rottemerentunnel opened in October 2025 and is monitored continuously from Rhoon; controllers can close it and operate incident systems. This supersedes the 2025 municipal document's pre-opening lifecycle and supports retaining the generated A16 link, but not assuming event-time availability.

Monthly CC0 NWB produces eight municipal-border logical links: A12 to Zuidplas and Zoetermeer, A16 and N209/N471 to Rotterdam, N209 toward Alphen aan den Rijn, and N470/N471 to Pijnacker-Nootdorp. Repeated A12, N209 and N471 endpoints are series ends of physical corridors, not additive capacity; nominal 260/150 values are scenario ceilings, not observed throughput.

ProRail contains Lansingerland-Zoetermeer station and GTFS contains 55 stop areas, including Station Lansingerland-Zoetermeer, Berkel Westpolder and Rodenrijs Metro. Static rail, station, stop and schedule geometry does not establish train/metro/bus operation, accessibility, loading, crew, emergency use or restoration.

The road skeleton omits internal approaches, tunnel-system dependencies, grade-separated and rail/metro crossings and role-specific care/supply routes. The deployment assigns no intersecting current NDW record; absence in one 72-hour snapshot is NoData, never proof that every corridor or tunnel is open.

evidenceSources.publisher: RIVM / Stichting Mijn Aansluiting / Netbeheer Nederland / RDI / DUO / KNMI / Rijkswaterstaat
evidenceSources.title: E07 — Acute-care, provider, grid-planning, antenna, education and current-observation context
evidenceSources.edition: RIVM acute-care v1.1 published 3 July 2026; other deployed snapshots retrieved 2–3 September 2026 and provider source dates vary
supports: RIVM's CC0 2026 v1.1 questionnaire assigns no acute-care point inside GM1621. Straight-line context from the generated centre places Franciscus Gasthuis Rotterdam at about 6.9 km, HagaZiekenhuis Zoetermeer 7.7 km and IJsselland Capelle aan den IJssel 8.2 km; all report 24/7 SEH and acute obstetrics. Registration and annual activity do not establish route travel time, acceptance, occupancy, staff, backup, diversion or incident capacity.

Public Domain Mijn Aansluiting point lookup identifies Stedin electricity (source updated 24 March 2026), Stedin gas (17 December 2025), Dunea drinking water (12 May 2026) and Ziggo media (7 September 2025); drainage is empty. One point is not complete municipal territory, physical topology, live state, quality, capacity or restoration.

One NBNL planning sample, TT114_10 Bergschenhoek, reports null existing/required withdrawal and injection values, queue counts zero, TenneT categories 3/0 and 12 projects with earliest year 2026. Zero queued requests does not mean spare capacity; null values remain Unknown. The product is described as open data but no exact dataset-licence identifier was found, and it is planning context rather than outage telemetry or project completion.

RDI supplies 98 antenna records (40 mobile, 34 fixed link, 23 amateur and one broadcast) and daily CC-BY DUO RIO supplies 41 education records (27 primary, six secondary and eight other). Neither proves coverage/backhaul/power, shelter designation, occupancy, staffing, supplies or restoration; the RDI service exposes no standard licence or cadence in consumed metadata.

The bounded deployment assigns no local Waterinfo observation/forecast, NDW record, KNMI weather observation/warning or seismic origin, or RIVM PM2.5 point. Empty coverage is source-, time- and geometry-specific NoData, not normal water/weather/air, open roads, zero seismic hazard or safety; the KNMI warning product also stops at 48 hours.

evidenceSources.title: E08 — Regional kering scenario, current crisis governance and dated Rottemeren nature-fire status
evidenceSources.edition: Crisisplan 2026–2029 adopted 10 December 2025; earlier risk-profile scenario retained as historical planning context; municipal fire notice dated 13 August 2026
supports: The VRR board adopted Crisisplan 2026–2029. Its minutes describe 72-hour municipal crisis-team self-sustainment as a guideline/goal that was not then current reality for smaller municipalities and required capacity/financial follow-up. This is not evidence that Lansingerland has or lacks a particular resource; no 72-hour autonomy or recovery should be assumed.

An earlier VRR regional-risk scenario explicitly uses the 2011 Lansingerland dike-weakening incident and distinguishes a regional-kering breach after drought and extreme rain, compartmentation, emergency measures, communication and possible evacuation of non-self-reliant residents. Its planning period is not current, its approximately 0.25 m street-depth narrative is a scenario rather than an observation, and it cannot calibrate a generic river preset.

The municipality reported on 13 August 2026 that Staatsbosbeheer prohibited open fires and barbecues in Rottemeren from 12 August because prolonged drought coincided with regional nature-fire phase 2. The page states no end time. It is a dated risk/action notice, not proof of a current ignition, flame footprint, spread forecast or indefinite validity.

Municipal guidance names NL-Alert, Rijnmond Veilig, sheltering, crisis communication, regional partners and emergency mayoral powers. Preparedness guidance and legal capability are not confirmed incident actions; an operational ledger must identify authority, event, issue/valid time, resource, target, status and completion. No standard blanket machine-reuse licence was identified.

emergencyContext.summary: Official water, drought, fire and crisis sources define mechanisms and roles but not a selected live incident or response state.

The 72-hour capability reference is a guideline/goal, not proof of municipal autonomy, resource availability or recovery.
Plans, legal powers, notices and works remain affectsSimulation=false unless a governed event/action adapter binds authority, issue/valid time, state and completion.

scenarioMatrix.summary: All ten presets, six checkpoints and eight services execute deterministically for GM1621.
notes: Initial focused model audit passed both tests across the complete matrix.

Outputs are synthetic exercise indices: affected people-equivalent is not observed people/casualties, floodDepthM is unsupported local precision without a governed event, and deprived person-hours is weighted local service deprivation versus a matched baseline.

numericalInvariants.summary: Determinism, finite bounds, zero-event behavior, reconciliation and monotonic burden contracts pass.
notes: All availability values remain in [0,1]; repeat runs, zero-intensity controls and UI/core preset equality pass.
Local population, demand and delivery reconcile exactly and event-attributable deprived person-hours is monotonic.
Initial focused gate passed 2/2 tests in 29.12 seconds; a diagnostic probe enumerated T+24/T+72 outputs and was removed.
Arithmetic correctness does not establish local event selection, physical calibration or operational truth.

spatialPlausibility.summary: Major-river, tidal/regional-kering and pluvial pathways are conflated, while unrelated hazards reuse population-led local ordering.
notes: River holds floodDepthM 1.464364, severity 0.457212 and 29,938 affected from T+24 through T+72 without a selected Rhine/Meuse branch, Nieuwe Maas/Rotte boundary, downstream backwater, kering, regional-defence failure, storage or inundation footprint.

Coastal T+24 reports 1.467932 m and pluvial 0.602696 m without respectively resolving sea/tidal boundary and defences or rainfall, terrain, groundwater, sewers, catchments, receiving levels, pumps and controls.

Storm, pluvial, river, heat, winter, cyber and wildfire all rank Oosteindsche Ackers and Dorp Bergschenhoek first and second; storm, pluvial, river, coastal, heat and wildfire share the same top five, which then follow the largest neighbourhood populations. This cannot represent mechanism-specific water, heat, wind/ice, cyber or smoke geography.

Wildfire has zero direct flame with synthetic smoke/drought despite no selected ignition; earthquake has zero T+24 ground motion with nonzero burden. The zeros are narrow model outputs, not local all-clears.

serviceDependencies.summary: Eight service balances calculate, but water-control, utility, access, care and greenhouse/supply topology and state are absent.
notes: At river T+24 availability is power 0.506571, water 0.483268, drainage 0.343740, gas 0.688597, telecom 0.458378, mobility 0.716477, facilities 0.413127 and supply 0.719840; at compound T+24 it is 0.377436, 0.386915, 0.313261, 0.509524, 0.240424, 0.738280, 0.348368 and 0.792260. No operator validates these exact values.
NWB route links are logical Mobility and assumed road-logistics Supply context only, not power, drinking-water, wastewater, gas, telecom, care or pump/kering topology.

The Rotte/Schilthuis/Eendragtspolder chain, split HHSK/Delfland system, Kralingseveer dependency, 349 water objects, provider point territories, Bergschenhoek grid-planning sample, antennas, schools and external hospitals provide context but no compatible connectivity, load/flow, state, backup, staff, stock, crew or repair evidence.
The graph does not propagate Rottemerentunnel systems, rail/metro/access interruption, external hospital acceptance/diversion or greenhouse water/power/fuel/logistics dependencies.

causalTrace.summary: Synthetic ledgers close and public context remains non-causal, but no locally selected event or action supports the consequences.
notes: Hazard contributions sum to severity; service-stage deltas close to availability; weighted service-loss contributions close to pressure; local demand/delivery and municipal totals reconcile.
Preparedness/intervention stages affect consequences rather than hazard fragility, while official scenarios, plans, registers, observations, notices and works remain affectsSimulation=false.

The trace selects no Rotte/New Maas boundary, kering/kade failure, rainfall/drainage state, fire ignition, cyber target, tunnel/route state, operator topology, hospital acceptance or authority action.

Arithmetic closure explains a synthetic exercise only; it cannot convert project intent, a historic scenario, a dated phase notice, a provider point or an empty current dataset into causation or safety.

recovery72h.summary: Frozen river/compound states and exact residual recovery lack hydraulics, operators, access and confirmed first-72-hour actions.
notes: River retains exactly floodDepthM 1.464364, severity 0.457212, 29,938 affected, pressure 0.461653 and all eight service values from T+24 through T+72; burden reaches 2,031,763.83 without arrival, recession, dewatering, repair or action evidence.

Compound severity falls from 0.971152 to 0.634584, but floodDepthM 0.621540, 37,400 affected, pressure 0.541819 and all eight service values are exactly frozen from T+24 through T+72; burden reaches 2,482,335.21.

Coastal direct forcing clears by T+72, yet residual pressure 0.129516, exact service values and 1,784,707.24 deprived person-hours lack boundary recession, drainage, access and operator-action evidence.

Every plateau, persistence and recovery needs a typed event/action/resource ledger with authority, issue/observation/valid time, blocking state, assigned resource and completion evidence; 72 hours is a planning horizon, not a recovery or self-sufficiency promise.
